intro_html: Korma is the mild, creamy, slightly sweet curry that wins over just about everyone. Cashews and coconut milk make it feel indulgent while the numbers stay high protein and cheap per serving. One batch makes 14 servings.
cost_closing_html: About $3.81 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each of the 14 servings runs about 57g protein for roughly 584 calories, at around $2.08 a bowl.
upsell_html: Creamy, cozy, and crowd-pleasing, korma makes eating well all week feel like a treat. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: A little honey gives korma its signature gentle sweetness, so skip any pricier specialty sweeteners.
One bag of cashews does double duty as thickener and richness, which beats buying cream.
Buy the bulk chicken breast to keep this rich bowl budget-friendly.
make_it: Add the chicken breast, chopped onion, and minced garlic to the crock.
Stir in the tomato paste, coconut milk, chicken broth, and a spoonful of honey.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 hours until the chicken is tender.
Shred the chicken and stir it back into the creamy sauce.
Blend or crush the cashews and stir them in to thicken and enrich.
